review: Reviewed Lin's round-8 request 'Construct a simple weather shelter' and the World Agent's develop review (learning 4): a general 'Assemble and maintain a simple shelter' operation for a low single-person braced lean-to with a sloping roof (two forked posts, a ridge pole, four braces, six ribs, 12 m of binding, 3 m2 of overlapping roofing, at most 2 m2 of covered floor, ridge at most 1.2 m, slope at least 35 degrees), 12 paid increments at 1 energy each, partial rain and wind shielding of at most 50% and 35% for one occupant within light-weather limits, weather wear, inspection, repair, dismantling, cancellation and death rules, and no new experience reward. Registry reconciliation: the complete long-ex15 registry (19 abilities: foundation-forest, foundation-open, foundation-expression and food-preparation@1) has no construction or shelter ability; the earlier shelter packages (resting-shelter@1 ex10, weather-lean-to@1 ex11, weather-barrier@1 ex14) are scoped to other experiments, so none is installed or duplicated; gather, probe, pickup, learn and navigation remain the separate existing operations. Unlike ex14's weather-barrier@1 first release, the specification is self-consistent, so this is a simplified but real mechanism, not a first release. Implemented simple-shelter@1 in scope long-ex15 with modes start, resume, cancel, inspect, repair and dismantle. Start takes x, y, orientation and exact owned untreated whole units totalling 13 branch, 4 vine and 6 bark, checks a 2 m x 2 m footprint (in reach, inside the world, ordinary '.' soil, waterlogging at most 0.1, no hazard, no overlap with solid or reserved objects, no living person), and reserves the materials through collective-work escrow as carried, owned pieces split per increment. Each paid increment (one round, 1 energy; start pays the first, the bound action continues) revalidates reach, reserved pieces, site waterlogging and occupancy, then moves that increment's pieces out of the stacks into persistent structure components with the same quantity, origin and age: 2 posts, 3 ridge and braces, 3 ribs and binding, 3 roofing courses of 2 bark, and a final increment that runs coded lateral-stability, binding-pull, roof-load and runoff checks; passing commissions the shelter and records the light-weather limits and the supported roof load (8.4 mass units), failing leaves it unverified. Too little energy, leaving reach, waterlogging or another occupant pause without charge; a round not worked pauses; a lost reserved piece stops the work and returns the survivors. Cancel (one round, no energy) returns uninstalled pieces once and leaves installed parts as an unfinished structure; death drops uninstalled pieces where the person died and leaves installed parts. Inspect (anyone who studied; one round, 0.2 energy) records an unverified personal record and reruns the checks, which can withdraw or restore protection. Repair (builder only; one round, 1 energy) replaces exactly one installed increment's parts with the same recipe of owned units, leaving the removed parts on the ground with their condition, and restores only those parts; protection lost to wear returns only after a passing reinspection. Dismantle (builder only; one round, 1 energy per stage) returns the last installed stage to the ground at the site with each part's condition; recovered parts can be reused at that condition. Effect: a new physiology hook (long-shelter-exposure.ts, inserted after the existing refuge and lean-to hooks in forest-environment.ts and inactive unless simple-shelter@1 is installed, so ex7-ex14 are unchanged) adds back exposure x (rain x rainShield + wind x windShield) of the existing outdoor exposure chill for exactly one living person wholly on the 2 m x 1 m covered floor of a commissioned shelter, with rainShield = 0.5 x roof condition x the body share whose wind-slanted rain ray meets the roof plane and windShield = 0.35 x roof condition x max(0, cos(orientation)); the body temperature then evolves through the existing update. Weather above 0.8 rain or wind, water pooling on the floor, a second person, the open side facing the wind, an unfinished, unverified or unsafe structure, or an enclosure already removing the chill give no protection; copies never stack; air temperature, hunger, nutrition and rest are unchanged. Each round installed parts wear by 0.0005 + 0.002 x rain + 0.002 x wind (the ex11 weather-lean-to law); a part below condition 0.5 makes a commissioned shelter unsafe. Events: simple-shelter-started, -progress, -paused, -resumed, -cancelled, -failed, -test-failed, -commissioned, -inspected, -deteriorated, -damaged, -repaired, -dismantled and -exposure-measured, all carrying the structure or work id; the structure's data.view holds reusable drawing metadata (component shelter, footprint, covered floor, orientation, slope, ridge height, installed components with resource colors and condition, roof coverage, stage, visible damage, status). No satisfaction rule, practice milestone (the commissioning event carries no qualified flag) or other reward is added. Modeling assumptions: one whole branch unit is one usable member of the required size (branch records have no length or diameter); one vine unit is 3 m of binding (the ex10 vine length law); one bark unit covers 0.5 m2 of overlapped roofing (the ex11 six-bark lean-to roof); ordinary '.' soil with waterlogging at most 0.1 permits hand insertion of forked posts to 0.3 m, and falling-object hazards and runoff channels are represented only by the ground type and waterlogging; the declared geometry is a 2 m ridge at 1.2 m over a 1 m deep floor, a slope of about 50 degrees; the material checks use the existing constitutive values probe reveals (branch strength 0.3, vine flexibility 0.9, bark water resistance 0.9) and the parts' current condition, so they fail only after wear; world wind has no direction, so the prevailing wind and wind-driven rain are taken to come from +x with a horizontal slant of 0.25 x wind per unit of fall, the convention of the existing ex10 open-refuge exposure solver; people have no wetness state in this world, so rain wetting is reduced through the rain part of the existing exposure chill; light weather means rain and wind at most 0.8, the frozen full-pressure rain amplitude of this scenario; protection scales with roof condition; with two or more people on the floor nobody is protected; only the builder may repair or dismantle because no access transfer is represented; posts are not separate collision bodies and the footprint is a reserved non-solid area; there is no dedicated viewer drawing, so the viewer's generic fallback shows the footprint colored by roof coverage. Reuse: collective-work.ts (escrow, paid work, stop), material-lots.ts, open-physical.ts (ground conditions and constitutive values), forest-climate.ts (rain, wind, outdoor chill), open-foundation.ts (personal records), the ex11 wear law and the ex10 wind-driven rain convention. Tests (apps/simulator/test/long-ex15-simple-shelter.test.ts, 11 cases, materials gathered by real gather actions) cover the ex15-only scope and four-round study, 12 rounds and 12 energy with per-increment installation and exact conservation and load transfer, measured shielding equal to the body-temperature difference against an unprotected copy with unchanged air temperature, satiety and energy, no wind protection with the open side to the wind, no protection for two occupants, off the floor or beyond the light-weather limits, pausing and resuming without charge, cancellation, rejected starts that spend nothing, builder-only rules, wear to unsafe followed by exact repair and reinspection, stage-by-stage dismantling and death. Development-3 was rejected by the handoff validator because the package declared its simple-shelter visual component before the viewer implemented it; this resubmission (development-4, a separate counted attempt) adds a small viewer drawing (footprint, ridge, installed roof courses, dashed until commissioned) and changes nothing else.
